tasks.task: Test the functionality of starting a new game.
tasks.expected: The game should initialize with an introductory screen displaying instructions on how to play, including sorting waste into correct containers.

tasks.task: Check the leaderboard feature to ensure it displays scores correctly.
tasks.expected: The leaderboard should show a list of players with their respective scores in descending order without any visual errors.

tasks.task: Assess the cartoon-style visual design for appropriateness.
tasks.expected: The visuals should be colorful, child-friendly, and consistent throughout the website, with no inappropriate or non-cartoonish elements present.

tasks.task: Test the feedback system for incorrect sorting.
tasks.expected: Placing a waste item in the wrong container should trigger a gentle correction prompt explaining the correct choice without being discouraging.

tasks.task: Verify the awarding of rewards and recognition within the game.
tasks.expected: After correctly sorting a designated number of items or reaching a specific score, the game should display a reward screen or badge to acknowledge the player’s achievement.

tasks.task: Verify that the website uses 'seashell' as the background color and 'crimson' as the component color, as specified in the design requirements.
tasks.expected: The website has a background color of 'seashell' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'crimson', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

tasks.task: In the Avatar Studio, type 'Z' into the nickname field, then add more letters to make it 'Ziggy'.
tasks.expected: With just 'Z' saving is blocked with a friendly note (names need 2-12 characters); once it reads 'Ziggy' the block lifts and saving becomes possible.

tasks.task: In the Avatar Studio, type 'greengreta' into the nickname field.
tasks.expected: The name is rejected as already taken even though it's typed in lowercase, and saving stays blocked with a friendly message.

tasks.task: In the Avatar Studio, click a different animal and then a different accessory without saving.
tasks.expected: The big preview updates immediately after each click, showing the newly chosen animal and accessory.

tasks.task: Type the lowercase nickname 'ziggy' in the Avatar Studio, pick the frog, save, then open the leaderboard page.
tasks.expected: The saved buddy appears at the top of the leaderboard page showing the frog avatar and the name as ZIGGY in all caps, despite being typed lowercase.

tasks.task: Open the leaderboard from the main screen.
tasks.expected: Players are listed with their scores in descending order, highest first.

tasks.task: Open the My Journey page and look at the overall accuracy stat.
tasks.expected: It reads 80.6% — computed as 58 correct out of 72 total items across the six seeded rounds, not 78.2% (the average of the per-round percentages).

tasks.task: On the My Journey page, look at the best-round spotlight.
tasks.expected: It shows the Kitchen Cleanup round with 260 pts and 14 of 15 correct (93.3%) — the score tie with the other 260 pts round is broken by accuracy.

tasks.task: Scroll the rounds list on the My Journey page.
tasks.expected: All six seeded rounds appear newest first — the 90 pts Park Patrol at the top and the 180 pts Park Patrol at the bottom.

tasks.task: Look at how every score is written on the My Journey page — averages, recent form, and each round in the list.
tasks.expected: Every score carries the pts suffix (all-time average 191.7 pts, recent form 190 pts, rounds like 260 pts) — and recent form is visibly a different number from the all-time average.

tasks.task: In the Avatar Studio, type 'greengreta' into the nickname field.
tasks.expected: The name is rejected as already taken even though it's typed in lowercase, and saving stays blocked with a friendly message.

tasks.task: Open the Recycle City map fresh.
tasks.expected: Park, Kitchen and School are open while Factory is the only locked spot — School counts as open because a Kitchen round hit 250 pts, even though School has never been played.

tasks.task: On the map, click the locked Factory spot.
tasks.expected: It shows a padlock and states the exact requirement — a School round reaching 250 pts — rather than opening the game or crashing.

tasks.task: Click the School spot and view its intro.
tasks.expected: The intro lists school-themed items such as crumpled paper, juice boxes and broken crayons — a different pile from Park's — along with a start button.

tasks.task: Enter Park from the map, start the round, sort one item, press the Done button, then open My Journey.
tasks.expected: A new round tagged Park sits at the top of the history, above the six seeded rounds.

tasks.task: Open the My Journey page and look at the overall accuracy stat.
tasks.expected: It reads 80.6% — computed as 58 correct out of 72 total items across the six seeded rounds, not 78.2% (the average of the per-round percentages).

tasks.task: On the Impact Calculator, type 7 into the aluminium cans box.
tasks.expected: Without pressing anything else, energy saved shows 1.40 kWh and TV hours shows 21 — the results update as you type.

tasks.task: On the Impact Calculator, type a number into the aluminium cans box, then clear it out completely.
tasks.expected: The results treat the empty box as zero and show clean numbers — no NaN, blank, or frozen values.

tasks.task: Look at the lifetime line at the top of the Impact Calculator.
tasks.expected: It says 58 items sorted right — the total correct sorts across the six seeded journey rounds, not 72 (the total items faced).

tasks.task: Start a game, sort exactly one item correctly, press Done, then return to the Impact Calculator.
tasks.expected: The lifetime line now reads 59 — it grew by exactly the one correct sort banked from that round.

tasks.task: In the Avatar Studio, click a different animal and then a different accessory without saving.
tasks.expected: The big preview updates immediately after each click, showing the newly chosen animal and accessory.

tasks.task: Open the Sticker Shop for the first time.
tasks.expected: The spendable balance shows 22 stars — only the four seeded rounds at or above three-quarters accuracy bank spendable stars (4+6+7+5, with the 9-of-12 round counting because it sits exactly on the bar), not 27 (the plain sum of all six rounds' stars) — and all five stickers are listed with none owned.

tasks.task: Buy the Diamond Turtle sticker (22 stars).
tasks.expected: The purchase goes through since it costs exactly the balance; the balance drops to 0 and every remaining sticker becomes unbuyable.

tasks.task: Buy the Super Worm sticker (3 stars), then try to buy it again.
tasks.expected: After the first purchase the balance reads 19 and Super Worm shows as owned; a second purchase of the same sticker is impossible.

tasks.task: Start a game, sort one item correctly with no mistakes, press Done, then open the Sticker Shop.
tasks.expected: The balance now sits above 22 — higher by exactly the stars that round banked, since the mistake-free round clears the three-quarters accuracy bar.

tasks.task: Open My Journey and then the Sticker Shop.
tasks.expected: Both pages show the soft aqua background and deep teal primary buttons with white text — neither page is left on the old seashell/crimson look.

tasks.task: Visit the Recycle City map, My Journey, and the Sticker Shop and look at each page heading.
tasks.expected: Every heading is centered with the wave mark in front of it, consistently on all three pages.

tasks.task: On My Journey, find the total stars banked.
tasks.expected: It still reads 27 and now sits on a small gold circle badge.

tasks.task: On the restyled map, click the locked Factory spot.

tasks.task: Open the Challenge Builder's first step.
tasks.expected: The target score field comes pre-filled with 260 — the best score in the journey — not blank, zero, or the most recent round's score.

tasks.task: In the builder, type 40 as the target score, then change it to 500.
tasks.expected: 40 gets a friendly rejection since the range is 50-500; 500 is accepted because the ends are included.

tasks.task: Pick the Kitchen pile, type 8 items and a 300 target, and continue to the review step.
tasks.expected: The review echoes Kitchen, 8 items and 300 pts, and lists the reward as 6 stars (one per full 50 pts).

tasks.task: Build a challenge with the Kitchen pile, continue past review, start it, press Done right away, then open My Journey.
tasks.expected: The finished round appears at the top of the journey history tagged as a Challenge.

tasks.task: On the Impact Calculator, type a number into the aluminium cans box, then clear it out completely.
tasks.expected: The results treat the empty box as zero and show clean numbers — no NaN, blank, or frozen values.

tasks.task: Open the Fact Card Album fresh.
tasks.expected: It shows 6 of 12 cards collected (50%) — Park's three and Kitchen's three from the seeded rounds — not a count inflated by the repeated Park rounds.

tasks.task: Look at the Park group in the album.
tasks.expected: Exactly three Park cards appear, each shown once, even though the journey holds four Park rounds.

tasks.task: Look at the Factory group in the album.
tasks.expected: Its three cards sit face-down with a padlock and say a Factory round earns them — no blanks or crashes for a never-visited spot.

tasks.task: Open School on the map, start a round, press Done, then open the Fact Card Album.
tasks.expected: School's three cards flip to collected and the album count reads 9 of 12 (75%).
